summary: Box-free wave 4: (a) control-plane simplification review of the auto fork (balancer/migration/mode-shift — correctness/clarity, not bench-gated), (b) 3s-static portability map for all queued 2s candidates (verify anchors exist in 3s, list adaptations).

candidates.change: Close the IO-exit inbox-wedge window: keep mb->io_exiting=1 until the park checkpoint actually adopts PARKED (clear it next to accept_left at server.c:11336, not at 11791), add `atomic_load(&mb->inbox_n)==0` to the IO->PARKED guard, and have the refused/parked path drain any stranded inbox clients back out (re-handoff via tmGatherLiveDests) before parking.
candidates.mechanism: Step 4 clears io_exiting and requests PARK while ctx->mode is still TOMO_MODE_IO. In that window (and in the TOCTOU between another source's dest-validity check at 11774-11775 and its tmMigHandoff inbox push), tmGatherLiveDests/the per-client fallback see io_exiting==0 && mode==IO and select the parking thread as a migration DEST. The park guard checks only accept_left and listLength(server.clients[id]) — inbox conns live in mb->inbox, not clients[id] — so the thread parks with a live client in its mailbox. A parked thread runs clock_nanosleep only (no beforeSleepIO, no tmMigDrainInbox): the connection is wedged indefinitely, rescued only if the thread ever re-enters IO. Variant: if the conn arrives one pass earlier it gets ADOPTED after io_exiting was cleared, and the exit wedges forever in IO with exiting flag off (clients!=0 blocks park, step-2 re-marking no longer runs).
candidates.risk: Fix touches cross-thread visibility of io_exiting (make it an atomic/relaxed int while at it — today it is a plain int read by tmGatherLiveDests and tomoMigrateTest cross-thread). Draining the inbox at park needs the same re-validation loop as step 3; window is narrow so hard to repro, easy to test by forcing test-5 on two threads concurrently.

candidates.change: After an IO-exit, the listener is closed (t->fd=-1) and never re-bound, so a later PARKED->IO re-entry calls listen(-1) and is refused forever. Either re-bind a dormant socket (anetTcpServerBindOnly + anetNonBlock, exactly like tmSpawnSpare) inside tmMigLeaveAcceptGroup, or teach the IO-entry branch to handle fd<0 by binding before listen().
candidates.mechanism: tomoMigrateTest(5) picks the HIGHEST live io_slot — that is the spare whenever the spare is in IO. So the supported sequence PARKED->IO (test 1), IO-exit (test 5), PARKED->IO again fails at listen(ctx->io->fd==-1); the checkpoint logs 'refused shift' once and the spare is permanently IO-incapable while tomoSpareShift already returned 1 to the caller (target stored, adoption never lands — and per the 3.1c pending-gate, ALL further shift requests except ->IO now reject with 'transition pending', so the spare is bricked for EX too until restart).
candidates.risk: Re-bind can transiently fail (EADDRINUSE is impossible with SO_REUSEPORT siblings, but bind can still fail); on failure must roll target_mode back to PARKED rather than leave the 3.1c pending-state wedge. The pending-wedge secondary effect is the nastier half — verify with test 1/5/1 cycling.

candidates.risk: Option (2b) (direct EX->IO at checkpoint) runs the shard-empty assert on the poly thread while main believes the transition is a single hop — the 3.1c gate handles callers, but the drain's serverAssert(resid==0) crash-on-violation now fires inside an IO-entry, so log wording must distinguish. Main's plain store races an owner RMW — a C11 data race on a field the file's own discipline declares owner-written; the comment 'same thread as the autotuner — no race' is true for mig_load_ewma/mig_last_ops (main-owned) but false for this line. Practically benign (lost store = one extra decay tick on an empty-queue worker), but it is the one place the control plane violates its own single-writer rule, and it is one of the step-3.1 residue nits.

candidates.change: Three v2-full-mix landmines to annotate now (or cheaply fix): (a) tomoMigrateTest's in-progress guard reads listLength(mb->migrating_out) and mb->io_exiting from the main thread while the source io thread mutates them — non-torn but a stale read lets a second REBALANCE overwrite mb->batch_dest while the first batch is mid-flight, silently redirecting its remaining conns (handoff-time re-validation keeps it safe, not correct-as-specified); make the guard fields atomic-relaxed and say the redirect is accepted behavior. (b) mb->rr_cursor is a signed int incremented per handoff — `rr_cursor++ % nd` hits signed-overflow UB after 2^31 handoffs; make it unsigned. (c) The balancer's donor-signal ingress loop (t=1..io_threads-1) permanently excludes the spare's tm_io_sig slot while rob/wb loops include t==io_threads — inert in v1 (balancer stands down when the spare is IO) but the loops silently disagree the moment v2 lets IO-capable threads float; a one-line comment on each loop stating the v1 assumption prevents the miscount from shipping unnoticed.
candidates.mechanism: All three are spare-only/v1-only assumptions baked into loops and guards without a marker; none misbehaves under the v1 legal transition set, which is exactly why they will survive into v2 unless flagged.
candidates.risk: (a)/(b) are two-line changes with no behavior delta today; (c) is comment-only. Ranked last because every consequence is either theoretical (2^31 handoffs) or masked by v1 policy.

candidates.change: P1 pendingCommand freelist — ADAPT (major). All anchors exist verbatim (same assert at 6610, same reclaim branches, same argv-preserve reset at 6690-6698, gate now !io_threads_active && !custom_ifid_threads_active). But the 2s safety argument ('alloc and free both on the SAME IO thread') is BROKEN in strict 3s: wbDrainClient retires every fake via commandProcessed ON THE WB thread (server.c:10867, comment 'RETIRE on the WB (own freeback ifidx)'), so freePendingCommand runs on WB while acquirePendingCommand runs on the ifid parse thread. A freed-thread-indexed freelist strands every pcmd in WB-ifidx slots that never allocate. Required adaptation: a WB->ifid pcmd recycle ring mirroring the operand pattern that already exists two functions away — operandRecyclePush (networking.c:4077) / operandPoolPutRouted (:4088) / operandRecycleDrain (:4100, drained at server.c:2209 in beforeSleepIfid) — routed by the same oif = c->parent->owner_ifid already computed at networking.c:6734. Push must happen AFTER the existing argv operandPoolPutRouted loop (operands route independently); argv-array preservation on the recycled pcmd still works (only zfree(pcmd->argv) at 6744 is skipped). Non-strict/main-thread path (handleWorkerReplies legacy path for ifidx 0, server.c:1983+) frees on the ifid thread and can use a plain local freelist push. Extra 3s ring-header cost is the known 33-slot scan issue (wave3 wb3s rank-4) — bound the drain range like freebackDrainAll does for WB slots (server.c:9915-9918).
candidates.mechanism: Same 4-allocator-calls/op shave (2 zmalloc + 2 zfree per command, verified pool-disabled with ifid threads active), but the free-side now crosses a core (WB), so recycling additionally removes the jemalloc cross-thread free-to-remote-tcache path — potentially a slightly BIGGER win than 2s where both were same-thread tcache ops. The recycle-ring plumbing (ring slot + release store per pcmd, one drain probe per ifid loop) eats some of it back.
candidates.risk: Higher than 2s: two producer classes (WB via ring, main/ifid via local push) must both cap and fall back to zfree; ring-full fallback must zfree (not leak); teardown path (freeClient on main after tid flip) still frees on main — bound-check ifidx like operandPoolPut. ASAN+CHURN gate mandatory (this file's refcount-race history). The 2s verify amendments (index by freeing thread, hook at freePendingCommand level, replicate argv-preserve reset, keep cmd_pool separate) all still apply.
